title: Tracking visited nodes when traversing datastructure

It mentions avoiding cycles (or repeat visits) when traversing structured data, eg nested structures or graphs or similar ("Beware of Cyclic Data Structures" at end of Ch 9). It suggests using a list/dictionary/set of already visited items. Clear enough. Set seems suitable. However if the data structure is composed of various mutable objects, these cannot be added in a Set, as python sets only take immutable (or perhaps hashable) objects, i.e. this pseudocode would not work: [CODE] What is a good way to do this, in python style? Some ideas: 1: Use a set to track id(obj) rather than object references themselves. However my impression is that id() is kind of an internal python implementation detail, so using it seems a bit hack-ish. [CODE] 2: Add a unique index attribute to each object in the datastructure/graph. Track that in the set. Simple enough if all objects are the same class, or at least are class instances. As far as I know it would not be possible if some nodes are lists for example. [CODE] 3: Use a list for visited. But it seems not ideal to use a list to emulate a set, when set is conceptually exactly what is wanted here.
